RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Skyler Foster
Member ID: W711189816
Reference Number: POC-BD05618334-73239
Date of Notice: 2026-08-19
Service/Procedure: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
Treating Surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Grievance and Appeals Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-19 (Reference POC-BD05618334-73239). This appeal is submitted within the 180-day window stated on that notice, which gives a deadline of 2027-02-15.

The notice states the reason for denial as follows: "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal together with the complete clinical record to address that stated deficiency directly.

Applicable policy
Based on my research, Anthem's prior-authorization and medical-necessity review of hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) is performed under the Carelon Medical Benefits Management (formerly AIM Specialty Health) document "Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines – Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Joint Surgery," Doc ID MSK02-1125.1, effective 11/15/2025 (the version in effect on the date of this denial). The denial notice itself did not identify a specific policy document or section by name or number. If a different document or version was actually used to review this request, I ask that Anthem identify it specifically and provide me a copy, consistent with my right to receive the criteria relied upon in an adverse benefit determination.

That guideline states the following general documentation standard, which I have retrieved directly from the current document:

"Providers may be required to submit clinical documentation in support of a request for services. Such documentation must a) accurately reflect the clinical situation at the time of the requested service, and b) sufficiently document the ordering provider's clinical intent. If these elements are not established with respect to a given request, the determination of appropriateness will most likely require a peer-to-peer conversation to understand the individual and unique facts that would justify a finding of clinical appropriateness."

The enclosed records satisfy both parts of that standard, item by item:

1. Symptom duration and severity: The record documents 18 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest, with sharp anterior groin pain on sitting and pivoting, and inability to run or squat. In the same guideline document, the hip arthroscopy/femoroacetabular impingement syndrome (FAIS) criteria that I was able to retrieve include the following language (quoted exactly as retrieved, though I was not able to retrieve this bulleted list in full and cannot confirm every remaining bullet under this heading):
"Moderate to severe hip pain (primarily in the groin) worsened by flexion activities (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) that interferes with activities of daily living, which is not explained by another diagnosis."
The documented symptoms match this description.

2. Functional limitation: The patient cannot run or squat and has pain with sitting and pivoting, directly supporting the "interferes with activities of daily living" language quoted above.

3. Conservative treatment attempted, with type and duration: The record documents 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization and activity modification (2026-03-31 to 2026-07-21, 18 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note); 6 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-26 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. This documents both the type and the duration of conservative measures tried.

4. Physical examination findings: The record documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. This corresponds to the following language from the same guideline, which I retrieved directly:
"Positive impingement sign on clinical examination, defined as pain elicited with 90 degrees of flexion and internal rotation and adduction of the femur OR with extension and external rotation."

5. Imaging findings: MRI arthrogram of the hip dated 2026-07-21 shows an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees, with preserved joint space and Tönnis grade 0. I was not able to retrieve the guideline's specific numeric imaging thresholds for cam-type impingement (e.g., the exact alpha-angle cutoff), so I am not attributing any particular threshold to the plan here; I note only that the treating surgeon has interpreted these findings as consistent with cam-type FAIS, and the absence of arthritis (Tönnis grade 0, preserved joint space) removes any concern about advanced osteoarthritis as a basis for exclusion.

6. Absence of contraindicating factors: The record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status. I have not located specific plan or guideline language listing these as exclusionary or qualifying criteria for hip arthroscopy, so I offer this information in my own words as background rather than as a quotation of any policy provision.

7. CPT correlation: The requested procedure, CPT 29914, is described in the same guideline's code table (confirmed in the current and adjoining versions of this Carelon document) as: "Arthroscopy, hip, surgical; with femoroplasty (i.e., treatment of cam lesion)." The imaging finding of cam-type impingement with an alpha angle of 68 degrees directly correlates to this code.

Because the stated reason for denial was incomplete documentation rather than a specific unmet clinical criterion, I ask that Anthem now review the complete record enclosed with this appeal — symptom history, functional limitations, physical therapy discharge summary, medication and injection records, physical examination findings, and the MRI arthrogram report — and reverse the denial of CPT 29914.

If any specific item is still considered missing, I ask that Anthem identify exactly what additional documentation is needed, and I ask Dr. Lindqvist's office be given the opportunity for a peer-to-peer conversation, which the same guideline document expressly contemplates as the mechanism for resolving cases where the reviewer believes required elements are not established.

Enclosed with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (16 weeks, 18 visits, 2026-03-31 to 2026-07-21)
- Medication trial records (NSAID therapy, 6 months)
- Corticosteroid injection record (2026-04-26)
- MRI arthrogram report and images (2026-07-21)
- Physical examination notes documenting provocative testing and range of motion
- Letter of medical necessity from Lindqvist, MD
- [Copy of the original prior authorization request and denial notice]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and provide the name and specific document (title, number, and effective date) of the medical policy or clinical guideline actually applied to this determination, if different from the Carelon "Joint Surgery" guideline (Doc ID MSK02-1125.1, effective 11/15/2025) identified above. Please also confirm the outcome of this appeal in writing before the 2027-02-15 deadline referenced in the original notice.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Skyler Foster
